title: observability: add token-level KV cache metrics, tracing, dashboards, and alert tuning
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add token-level KV cache metrics and tracing; new Grafana dashboard for token cost/latency breakdowns; tuned Prometheus alerts for KV cache hitrate and tail latency. Backwards-compatible metric names; rollout by feature flag.
description:
Motivation: several customer incidents and internal perf investigations showed we lacked visibility into token-level KV cache behavior and its impact on per-token latency and cost. This PR adds token-level KV cache metrics, tracing spans, a Grafana dashboard with cost/latency breakdowns, and tuned Prometheus alerts so SREs can detect regressions earlier.

What this PR does: 
- Instrument token-level KV cache metrics: rv_kv_cache_hits_total, rv_kv_cache_misses_total, rv_kv_cache_hit_rate (gauge), rv_kv_cache_miss_latency_seconds (histogram), rv_token_processing_latency_seconds (histogram labeled by cache_hit)
- Add tracing spans around KV cache lookup paths and token emit paths for improved distributed traces 
- New Grafana dashboard: dashboards/grafana/token_kv_cache_cost_latency.json summarizing cost-per-token, median/p95/p99 token latencies split by cache_hit/cache_miss, and cache hit-rate heatmaps by model/route 
- Prometheus alert tuning: create alert rules for low cache hit-rate, rising p99 token latency correlated with cache misses, and sudden increase in per-token cost. Thresholds chosen from 90th percentile of production baseline (see linked runbook).
- Tests: unit tests for metric exports and integration smoke for dashboard panel data.
- Rollout: feature-flagged (obs.kv_token_metrics) default off in Private deployments; enabled for 20% traffic in dedicated/hosted initially.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add metrics and histograms 
- [x] Add tracing spans and context propagation 
- [x] Grafana dashboard panels + templates 
- [x] Prometheus alert rules + runbook links 
- [x] Unit/integration tests 
- [x] Docs + migration notes (docs/observability/kv-cache-metrics.md)

Notes on compatibility and privacy: all metric names are prefixed with rv_ and are non-sensitive; no user PII is emitted. Dashboard templates use model and route tags but not token contents.

Related: ENG-1124 (observability improvements), PM-204 (dashboard for customer facing incidents), SUP-987 (customer reported KV cache regressions). Runbook: https://internal.grafana.company/d/obs/kv-cache-runbook

review_comments: Diego Morales: Nice work, this addresses a big blindspot. A few requests: 1) make the p99 histogram buckets explicit and justified, 2) avoid high-cardinality labels on rv_token_processing_latency_seconds, and 3) add an aggregation for model family.

Author (Aisha): Thanks Diego updated histogram buckets to cover 1ms-10s with exponential buckets, removed route-level cardinality from the latency histogram and added model_family label with coarse granularity. See commit b9f2a11 and registry changes.
Ben Carlson: Can we ensure alerts are noisy-resistant? I see a potential for noisy alerts during deploys. Suggest adding a 10m for p99 and require hit-rate drop for 5m with increased traffic check.

Author (Aisha): Added alert for sustained 5m hit-rate drop combined with 10m p99 increase and a suppression during canary windows using alertmanager inhibited rules. See monitoring/prometheus/alerts/kv_cache_alerts.yml.
Lina Zhang: Tests look good, but please add an e2e smoke for a small local workload showing cache hit/miss labeling works in traces.
Author (Aisha): Added integration-tests/observability/smoke_kv_metrics.test to simulate warm cache hits and cold misses and assert metrics + spans are emitted.
Diego Morales: Approve after the above fixes.
